findings.message: This drops `bundle_name` from the DagModel UPDATE, which is a behaviour change rather than a cost saving: a Dag whose file has moved to a different bundle and now fails to parse keeps its stale bundle_name instead of being re-pointed. Since `import_errors` is now keyed by (bundle, filename) the right fix is probably to write the per-key bundle rather than to stop writing it — and either way nothing in the new tests covers the DagModel side of this statement.

The comment concedes the table still gets scanned because there is no index on (bundle_name, filename), so what this buys is fewer ORM rows built, not a cheaper query — and it swaps an unfiltered scan for a scan plus a row-value IN with 2 bind parameters per entry. Worth saying in the PR description what `import_errors` realistically holds per call; if it can carry a whole bundle's worth of broken files, this wants chunking (and an index is the actual fix for the scan).
